answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample of its claims against independent evidence. If an audit finds fabricated results, the protocol burns the bond and excludes the identity; creating a swarm of accounts therefore multiplies the capital at risk, rather than multiplying influence for free. The bond need not stop every attack, but makes Sybil farming costly: an attacker must tie up funds and may lose them, whether the agents wander after a comet or crowd the zenith.
